newsitem.title: USA: Best Buy computer writedown due to pricing.
newsitem.headline: Best Buy computer writedown due to pricing.

text.p: Best Buy Co Inc said Wednesday it took a charge against fiscal third quarter earnings to cover a write-down of personal computer inventories, and this resulted in an overall loss for the quarter.
The charge was mainly due to current pricing conditions rather than excess levels of inventory, the consumer electronics retailer said.
Best Buy reported a net loss for the third quarter, ended November 30, of about $11 million, or $0.25 a share, after a pre-tax charge of $15 million, or $0.21 a share.

Best Buy said its merchandise inventories totaled $1.85 billion at November 30, compared to $1.97 billion a year earlier. The reduction in inventory levels, despite the addition of 21 new stores this year, was almost entirely due to reduced buying and tighter control of personal computers in anticipation of the upcoming model transition, the retailer said.

In the company's fiscal year 1996, new computer models were introduced in February. In the current fiscal 1997, the introduction came six weeks earlier. The timing of this transition has caused computer prices to decline during the busiest months of the year, Best Buy said.

The market for personal computers continues to be highly promotional, with sizable price reductions, free merchandise and financing offers used to stimulate consumer demand, Richard Schulze, Best Buy chairman and chief executive officer, said in a statement. This resulted in extreme margin pressure beginning in November and continuing through December, he said.

The promotional behavior by manufacturers and retailers is caused by the need to sell current models before the introduction of Intel's MMX microprocessor, expected after the first of the year, Schulze said.

In addition, consistent with trends reported earlier in the year, the consumer electronics and entertainment software categories have remained soft, further impacting sales and overall profitability, he said.
Best Buy is a specialty retailer of consumer electronics, personal computers and home office products, entertainment software and appliances. It operates 272 stores in 32 states.
Shares of Best Buy were off 1/4 to 12-1/4.
